results.description:
Sokoto: Bandits Shoot Resident, Rustle 28 Cattle Near UDUS

Armed bandits invaded Gidan Asarki, near Usmanu Danfodiyo University, Sokoto, around 9pm on Sunday, October 25, shooting a resident in the leg and stealing 28 cattle, police confirmed.

Residents said the attackers also threatened them and demanded that students living in the community be brought out. The victim is receiving treatment. No deaths or abductions were confirmed at the time of reporting.

JUST IN: 🇳🇬 
BANDITS KIDNAP PASSENGERS TRAVELLING FROM KEBBI TO ABUJA

Armed bandits have reportedly kidnapped more than 10 passengers travelling from Yauri, Kebbi State, to Abuja yesterday.

The vehicle's driver was also reportedly abducted.

In a disturbing video from the incident, one of the victims is seen calling his mother while a bandit points an AK-47 rifle at the abducted passengers.

results.title: Old Zamfara Wedding Video Recycled to Spread Fear as Nigerian Army Sustains Pressure on Terrorist Networks In North-West SpyeTV Fact-Check a
results.description:
Old Zamfara Wedding Video Recycled to Spread Fear as Nigerian Army Sustains Pressure on Terrorist Networks In North-West

SpyeTV Fact-Check and Security Analysis

The recirculation of an old video showing heavily armed men at a wedding ceremony in Zamfara State has raised fresh concerns over the deliberate use of recycled security-related footage to create panic, spread fear and undermine public confidence in ongoing military operations in Nigeria's North-West.

A fact-check of the footage indicates that the video is not a recent incident, contrary to the impression being created by some social media posts. The footage was reportedly first circulated widely around November 21, 2025, following a report by Sahara Reporters about armed men attending a wedding Fatiha reportedly linked to a notorious bandit kingpin in Zamfara State.

Although the exact town and precise date of filming have not been independently established, the available information points to an incident from 2025, not a fresh security development.

The video is therefore old footage being recirculated without adequate historical context, potentially misleading unsuspecting members of the public into believing that the incident has just happened.

This development raises an important question: why are some social media commentators and self-acclaimed influencers recycling old security videos at a time when troops are sustaining operations against terrorist groups across the North-West?

Recycled Footage and the Politics of Fear

What makes the development particularly disturbing is the manner in which some individuals operating under the labels of social media commentators, bloggers and influencers appear to exploit sensitive security-related content without verifying its date, origin or present relevance.

Rather than provide context, some accounts repost disturbing videos from previous incidents, sometimes without mentioning when or where the events occurred. The result is a misleading narrative capable of making Nigerians believe that terrorists are currently moving freely into communities or staging public gatherings without resistance.

Such conduct, when deliberate, goes beyond ordinary social media commentary. It can become a dangerous form of information manipulation, particularly in a region where thousands of residents have experienced kidnapping, displacement, attacks on communities and years of insecurity.

The North-West does not need manufactured panic. Its people need credible information, responsible journalism, effective security operations and sustained government intervention.

There is nothing wrong with criticising the government or demanding better security. Indeed, the media and citizens have a responsibility to question security failures. However, deliberately presenting an old video as a current attack, without disclosing its historical context, is not responsible criticism.

Those who genuinely desire peace should not turn the suffering of vulnerable communities into an opportunity to generate online engagement, attract followers or advance political and personal interests.

Operation FANSAN YAMMA: Sustained Pressure on Terrorist Networks

While old footage is being recirculated to create the impression that nothing is changing in the security situation, troops of the Nigerian Army and other security components under Joint Task Force North-West, Operation FANSAN YAMMA, have continued to mount pressure on terrorist networks across the region.

Recent operational records provide a different picture from the narrative that terrorists are having unrestricted access to communities and military-controlled areas.

On October 7, 2026, troops of Sector 2, Operation FANSAN YAMMA, repelled an attack by suspected Lakurawa terrorists on the Forward Operating Base in Maiyama, Kebbi State.

Freedom of expression comes with responsibility, particularly when information concerns the safety and security of millions of Nigerians.
